key_insight: Projected-Block Van Vleck Perturbation Theory (PB-VVPT) efficiently predicts quantum-state transfer in molecular polaritonic networks while capturing phonon-induced decoherence and fidelity revivals.
engineering_relevance: The method could accelerate simulation and design of cavity-coupled molecular quantum-state-transfer architectures without assuming memoryless environmental dynamics.
method: Model molecular excitons, an optical cavity, and local phonons with a generalized Holstein–Tavis–Cummings Hamiltonian.
Use PB-VVPT to reduce the Hamiltonian into fixed-phonon-number sectors and coupled polaron–polariton subblocks.
Compute coherence and population propagators, including phonon-induced renormalization, without a Markovian approximation.
evidence_signal: Against exact molecular-wheel simulations, PB-VVPT reproduced molecule-to-molecule and molecule-to-cavity transfer with errors below 1% over most simulated intervals and an estimated diagonalization cost more than 100 times lower.
watch_item: Validation is computational and assumes weak exciton–phonon coupling in the nonadiabatic regime; accuracy outside that regime remains unestablished.
paper_title: Quantum Information Transfer in Molecular Polaritonic Networks: A Van Vleck Effective-Hamiltonian Approach
